prompt: A slow-motion science-museum photo shows a straight left-to-right row of 13 identical standing dominoes, numbered 1 to 13 from the LEFT. Someone taps domino 1 so the row begins to topple, each falling domino knocking the next. The camera FREEZES the instant domino number 7 has just fallen flat but has not yet reached domino 8. Render that exact frozen frame: dominoes 1 through 7 lying flat (fallen), and dominoes 8 through 13 still standing upright. Show all 13 tiles in a single straight row, clearly distinguishing fallen (lying flat) from standing (upright). Do NOT print the numbers 7 or any tile labels on the image.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show slow-motion science-museum photo of a 13-domino row frozen at the instant one particular tile has fallen, the first seven flat and the last six upright? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_phys_form: Look only at the fallen dominoes lying down in this photo. Which option matches what is drawn: (a) the fallen dominoes lean on or overlap one another, or (b) they lie flat and separate, with clear gaps and none touching the next? Answer with the single letter a or b only.
reference.q_phys_len: Compare a fallen domino's length with a standing domino's height in this photo. Which option matches what is drawn: (a) a fallen domino is about as long as a standing one is tall, or (b) a fallen domino is clearly shorter or clearly longer than that? Answer with the single letter a or b only.
reference.q_notext: Is there any printed word or number anywhere on this photo? Answer yes or no only.
